**Audio Studio MCP 1.1 installs with one command.** It is now on PyPI, so there is nothing to clone: run `uvx --python 3.11 audio-studio-mcp setup` once (on Windows add `--torch-backend cu126`), then register the same command with your MCP client. It is also listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.kanaworksai-hue/audio-studio-mcp`. The install scripts still work as before.

[🎧 Listen to samples](https://kanaworksai-hue.github.io/audio-studio-mcp/) · [English](https://github.com/kanaworksai-hue/audio-studio-mcp#readme) · [简体中文](https://github.com/kanaworksai-hue/audio-studio-mcp/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](https://github.com/kanaworksai-hue/audio-studio-mcp/blob/main/README.ja.md)

## Changes to note first

- **Default output folder for package installs.** When Audio Studio runs from the published package (uvx, pip), generated audio goes to `~/AudioStudio`. Source installs (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`, `uv sync`) keep using `outputs/` in the repository, and `AUDIO_STUDIO_OUTPUT_DIR` still overrides both.
- **The model runtime is now a regular dependency on the two supported platforms.** On Apple Silicon the package depends on MLX, and on Windows on PyTorch 2.7.1, so no extra is needed. The `mlx` and `cuda` extras still exist (`cuda` is what Linux needs).
- **License:** unchanged (MIT). The package metadata now also lists the notices of the bundled IBM Plex Sans font (SIL OFL 1.1) and of the Kana images, which are not MIT-licensed.

## New: install with uvx

```bash
# macOS (Apple Silicon)
uvx --python 3.11 audio-studio-mcp setup
claude mcp add --scope user audio-studio -- uvx --python 3.11 audio-studio-mcp

# Windows (NVIDIA GPU)
uvx --python 3.11 --torch-backend cu126 audio-studio-mcp setup
claude mcp add --scope user audio-studio -- uvx --python 3.11 --torch-backend cu126 audio-studio-mcp
```

- **`audio-studio-mcp setup`** is the first-run guide. It checks the platform, downloads the official Stable Audio 3 runtime at the tested commit (about 1 MB is kept, in `~/Library/Application Support/audio-studio-mcp` or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\audio-studio-mcp`), tells you how big the model download is (macOS ~6.9 GB, Windows ~10.4 GB) and asks before downloading it. Interrupted downloads resume, files already in the Hugging Face cache are reused, and `-y` skips the question.
- **Windows:** setup checks the Hugging Face license and login before downloading. If something is missing it prints the steps (accept the license on the model page, then `uvx --from huggingface_hub hf auth login` in your own terminal) and stops. If uv installed the CPU-only PyTorch on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU (the command was run without `--torch-backend cu126`), setup and the server say so and show the command to use, instead of running very slowly on the CPU.
- **Apple Silicon with an x86_64 Python** (for example an old Intel Homebrew under Rosetta): the server and setup stop with the exact command to use instead (`--python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64`).
- **Before setup has run,** the server still starts, so your client connects, and every tool call answers with the setup command to run. A package install never downloads ~7 GB of weights inside a tool call that the client might time out.
- The README (English, 日本語, 简体中文) shows the setup for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, VS Code and Cursor, and has notes for AI agents that install it for you.
- `audio-studio-mcp --version` prints the version.

## Publishing

- Releases are published by GitHub Actions: publishing a GitHub release builds the package, uploads it to PyPI with Trusted Publishing and lists the version in the MCP Registry (GitHub OIDC). No tokens are stored in the repository.
- `server.json` describes the server for the MCP Registry, and the README carries the `mcp-name` marker the Registry uses to check that the PyPI package is ours.

## Web UI

- After you type a range by hand, the button changes to "Play selection" right away.
- The description box grows with its text (up to 40% of the window).
- Edit results are shown one sound per row; on narrow windows the row stacks.
- Result cards show your title, with the prompt as a subtitle.
- Wording that left one or two characters alone on the last line was rewritten, and long text no longer makes the result column wider than the window.

## Docs and development

- The README shows web UI screenshots in each language, in light and dark.
- `scripts/smoke_test.py --server "COMMAND"` runs the end-to-end test against another install, for example the built wheel through uvx.
- The weight download logic moved into the package (`audio_studio_mcp.weights`); `scripts/download_weights.py`, which the install scripts call, now uses it.
- CI: the Windows job retries the ffmpeg install and checks that it worked, and no longer installs the CUDA build of PyTorch, which the offline tests don't need.
